adds.title: LGBT rights in Chile
adds.summary: National framework document that applies to Arica y Parinacota. Chile's Gender Identity Law (Law 21,120, introduced 2013, enacted 2018) has since 2019 allowed people over 14 to change name and registered sex on all official documents, adults over 18 applying directly to the Civil Registry. Equal Marriage Law 21,400 came into force 10 March 2022, extending marriage and joint adoption to same-sex couples and guaranteeing non-discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in custody, filiation and adoption, while Law 20,609 (2012) bans discrimination on that basis and treats it as an aggravating criminal factor. The page's sourcing also records an Arica-specific precursor: the CAJTA legal clinic reported on 21 November 2016 that Arica courts had granted name and sex change to two people under the pre-statutory judicial route, evidence of how Arica's own courts handled gender recognition before 2019 that bears on this record's northern-judicial-climate framing.

adds.title: LGBT rights in Germany
adds.summary: National framework page applying to Bavaria. Adults have been able to change legal gender since 1980; the Self-Determination Act (Cabinet-approved August 2023; Bundestag vote 374-251 on 12 April 2024) lets adults over 18 change first name and gender by self-determination with three months' notice, in force since 1 November 2024. Same-sex marriage and adoption have been legal since 2017, and discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity is banned nationwide in employment and goods/services, though the page notes some protections vary by region. Supplies the federal legal baseline inside which Bavaria's own measures (the gender-language ban and the Länder push to tighten the SBGG) operate.

adds.title: Selbstbestimmungsgesetz
adds.summary: German Wikipedia article on the Self-Determination Act (SBGG), the federal law Bavaria's Bundesrat initiative sought to tighten. It passed the Bundestag on 12 April 2024 (374-251, 11 abstentions) and the Bundesrat on 17 May 2024, was gazetted 21 June 2024; changes could be registered from 1 August 2024 and took effect 1 November 2024. Adults declare the change themselves before the registry office; 14-17 year-olds need a guardian's (or the family court's) consent; for under-14s only the guardian can declare, and a three-month waiting period applies with a one-year lockout after a change. The article also records the Bundesrat's 20 October 2023 criticism that the draft let parents decide under-14 gender-entry changes 'without any counselling, examination and investigation of the child's welfare' - exactly the contested point behind the Bavarian-led tightening initiative this record covers.
